transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-11
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Liam (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Malik (Redwood CSM); Aisha (Sundial Eng Lead), Marco (Product), Chen (Infra), Jorge (ML)

Summary:
Quick sync on app integration status for the POC - focus on SDK usage, function/tool calling pattern, structured JSON output schema, and next steps for benchmark dataset and pricing. Discussed a few perf observations and security questions (KMS, SOC2). Agreed on concrete action items.

Topics:
- SDK integration progress and friction points
- Function-calling examples and tool orchestration
- Structured-output schema for downstream processors
- Latency/cost tradeoffs and batching settings
- Security/compliance follow-ups (KMS, logs, VPC)

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we will keep this to 40 minutes ish, go through updates and blockers. Priya and I will cover the SDK examples and then Malik will recap commercial next steps. Aisha, over to you for any updates on your side?
[00:22] Aisha: yeah thanks liam, we got the SDK wired into our staging app last week. overall pretty smooth, one snag: function calls sometimes return slightly different keys than the schema so our downstream parser fails, so we had to add a mapping layer.
[00:38] Priya: ok that mapping layer is something we expected - we can push a structured-output example that validates against a JSON schema and includes field-level types, the SDK supports schema enforcement at the call level so the model returns deterministic keys if you pass a schema object.
[00:53] Marco: is that the new SDK feature you demoed? i thought that was only in the hosted pipeline, can it run in Dedicated or Private?
[01:05] Priya: good question, schema enforcement is runtime-agnostic - it's a client-side hint plus a server-side enforcement in hosted. For Dedicated we give you the same behavior if you enable the structured-output flag in the deployment config; for Private it requires the feature flag and a slightly newer agent. basically yes, supported across modes but check version.
[01:25] Chen: quick infra note, when we tried the sample with our staging VPC we saw connection retries, seemed like a firewall/nat issue. If we move to VPC peering does Redwood need specific ranges or outbound rules?
[01:40] Liam: yeah we sent a checklist last month, but i'll resend. we need outbound ports 443, and for peering we'll provide the CIDR ranges for the peered subnets. I'll cc you the network guide and a trimmed firewall snippet.
[01:56] Aisha: perfect, thanks. on the functional side, can you explain the function-calling pattern you recommend if we have multiple internal tools (payments verifier, fraud check, enrichment)?
[02:10] Priya: sure - two patterns we see: 1) orchestration outside the model: you call the model for classification or text, then your app decides which tool to call; 2) function-call chaining: the model returns a structured call like {tool: "fraud_check", args: {...}} and Redwood routes or logs the tool calls through the SDK. Chaining can reduce round trips but you need good guardrails so model doesn't call arbitrary tools.
[02:34] Jorge: do you do any policy enforcement for allowed tools? we can't have the model call internal infra if it's not allowed.
[02:41] Priya: yes, the SDK includes an allowlist for tool IDs and you can configure per-route RBAC; calls are signed and logged. we also support a dry-run mode where we surface the suggested tool calls without executing.
[02:56] Marco: nice. what about batching? our traffic pattern for the POC is many small requests (user-initiated), so latency is critical but we also care about cost.
[03:10] Priya: exactly, the tradeoff. Redwood's runtime does continuous batching and you can tune the max latency window, or pin to low-latency configs. For user-facing flows we recommend small batch size + prefix caching to hit warm KV cache for repeated prompts. that reduces tokens and keeps latency within SLO.
[03:31] Chen: you mentioned KV cache earlier - how stateful is it? can we share across sessions?
[03:36] Priya: KV cache is per model instance and keyed by prefix; you can persist warm prefixes for common contexts. For Dedicated we can configure persistent KV cache on warm nodes; Private has options but requires disk-backed cache. We'll share a doc with exact limits.
[03:54] Aisha: on deterministic structured output - our downstream needs exact field names: transaction_id, amount_cents, currency, merchant_id, fraud_score. If the model sometimes returns camelCase vs snake_case we end up reprocessing. can you guarantee field shapes?
[04:15] Priya: guarantee is strong word, but with schema enforcement and a strict output template we get very high consistency. also you can enable post-assertion checks in the SDK - if the response doesn't match schema the request can be retried or flagged. that's what the example will show.
[04:34] Liam: also simple mitigation is to have the model emit a single JSON blob and then run a schema validator before downstream steps; that's what we recommend for pilot.
[04:44] Marco: ok good. any perf numbers from the last run? last week's run on staging showed avg latency 260ms but some tails were 900ms.
[04:54] Priya: right, the tail came from cold KV misses and occasional longer tool call latencies (we call external fraud service). If you pin a warm pool on Dedicated you'll see median ~120-150ms and tails under 300-350ms for the same model. For hosted the 95th can wiggle more.
[05:19] Aisha: what's the effort to pin a warm pool? we are evaluating Dedicated but haven't committed.
[05:25] Liam: for a pilot we can reserve a small Dedicated pool for a short term (30-day) and show the diff. I'll include short-term pricing for that option in the pilot pricing email.
[05:37] Chen: about logs and audit - we need request/response logs for debug but PII must be redacted and logs need to go to our SIEM. can Redwood push logs to our Splunk?
[05:49] Malik: yes, we support exporting audit logs via S3 + Kinesis and integrations with Splunk/Datadog. For PII we have automatic PII masking options and can also sign an addendum around retention. we'll share the security whitepaper link.
[06:06] Marco: can we get a sample webhook for function call events? we'd like to debug tool orchestration in our pipeline.
[06:12] Priya: yes, we'll add a sample webhook payload to the repo and a small simulator so you can reproduce chaining locally.
[06:21] Aisha: on the SDK itself - one pain was retries: when a function call error bubbled up the SDK did one retry but our tool is not idempotent. How do we control retry semantics?
[06:34] Priya: the SDK exposes per-tool retry policy and idempotency tokens; you can mark tools as non-retriable. Also we log the retry attempts. we'll add example config for your payments verifier.
[06:47] Jorge: quick question about model variants and quantization - we were testing gpt-like-7b-quant and saw a slight drop in fraud_score calibration. any best practices?
[06:57] Priya: smaller quantized variants can shift calibration; for classifiers we recommend running a small calibration step (a few hundred labeled cases) and we can apply a post-hoc calibration mapping. Redwood Optimize can suggest the right quantization profile for your dataset.
[07:15] Aisha: perfect. dataset - we'll share 50 sample cases that represent edge cases in fraud detection. anonymized. is 50 enough for an initial calibration?
[07:24] Priya: 50 is a good start for smoke and early tuning; for robust calibration we typically want 500+, but we'll get early signals from 50.
[07:33] Liam: ok so next steps roundup - Priya will add SDK examples, webhook simulator, and structured-output schema. Aisha will send sample data. i'll send pricing and dedicated options. Chen will validate infra and share network rules.
[07:46] Marco: timeline wise can we have the SDK examples by Friday?
[07:50] Priya: yes - i'll upload by Friday (2026-11-13) and ping in the repo.
[07:56] Liam: good. any blockers on legal or security to move pilot forward?
[08:02] Aisha: security team wants SOC2 report and confirmation about KMS integration - we need to know if keys stay in our cloud KMS or Redwood-managed keys.
[08:12] Malik: you can choose customer-managed KMS for Private/Dedicated; for hosted we support BYOK via Cloud KMS with envelope encryption. i'll share the KMS integration notes and SOC2 link.
[08:24] Chen: for peering we will need the exact CIDR ranges.
[08:27] Liam: noted, i'll send.
[08:30] Aisha: one more question: error handling for structured outputs - if model returns valid JSON but missing fraud_score, should we default to safe fail (block) or proceed? recommended pattern?
[08:41] Priya: recommended is fail-safe: if critical field missing, flag for human review or fall back to a deterministic rule. we'll include fallback patterns in the example.
[08:54] Marco: ok great. last bit - any competitor differentiation we should highlight for execs?
[08:59] Liam: two points: production-first controls (dedicated pools, KG cache tuning, rollout/AB testing) and cost-performance tooling (Optimize suggestions). Customers like the unified routing between hosted and dedicated which reduces rewrite.
[09:14] Aisha: sounds good.
[09:18] Liam: all right we'll wrap. Recap of action items and owners in the chat. Thanks everyone.

End of meeting - timestamp ~16:42 PT
